findings.message: Two different rules decide what counts as a 'move'. The card's Moves line, `releaseNote` and the checkbox detail (`movesOf` and `releaseProposals`) count a move only when `openElsewhere` is true, meaning the other release is not completed. `assignProposals` in services.ts pushes a `moved` entry whenever `p.release_id && p.release_id !== releaseId`, including when the other release is completed. That case also needs no `reassign`. So the service takes a proposal out of another release and audits `after.moved`, but the confirm card never showed that move. Fix: define the move once in release-proposals.ts and use it in both places. Either show moves out of completed releases on the card and in `option()`, or refuse/skip them in `assignProposals`. Add a test for the completed-release case.
findings.scenario: Proposal X is Verified and sits in R1 (category dev). R1 is completed by a Dev deployment. Create R2 with proposalKeys [X] and no reassign. The card shows no Moves line and X has no 'in R1' detail. The service still moves X out of R1 and the audit records moved:[{key:X, from:R1}]. A completed release loses a proposal with no warning on the card.

findings.message: The card's default version repeats pin-offers' 'latest release' query: `select version from delivery.release ... order by created_at desc limit 1`, also at pin-offers.ts:36. Both feed `nextVersion`. If one copy changes, the pin's 'Create release vX' label and the card's prefilled Version will disagree. Move the query into one shared helper.

The two tools parse proposal keys differently. `set_release_proposals` still declares `proposalKeys`/`reassign` as `z.array(z.string())`, while the service and `create_release` use `Keys`, which also accepts a comma-joined string. A comma-string from MCP is accepted by `create_release` but refused at `set_release_proposals`' tool boundary. Use `Keys` in both tool inputs.
